video_directives: Break up the long static holds (e.g., 'NOPE.' and 'SAHARA' scenes sit near-frozen 2-3s) with idle micro-motion — breathing, blinking, cloth sway
Add eased sub-beats inside diagram cards (ray path draws in, scattered-light rays pop sequentially) so cards feel alive instead of appearing fully-formed
Vary character blocking more between scenes — it currently slides left/right between backgrounds; add body turns, step-ins, or reactions timed to each new prop reveal

top3_directives: Kill the stray sunbeam that cuts vertically through the text block and the character's face — it reads as a rendering artifact, not a design choice
Fill the dead zone between 'THE OCEAN?' and the character (middle ~35% of frame) with a subtle atmospheric element or bump the character up slightly to tighten the eye path from hook text to subject
Give the subtitle 'THE OCEAN?' more size/weight separation from the header — right now it floats ambiguously and weakens the two-beat question setup
Fill the large dead sky zone in the upper half — the character sits low-center leaving ~40% empty blue; raise the composition or add secondary depth elements (distant umbrella, birds, towel)
Anchor 'NOPE.' into the composition — it floats mid-right with no connection to the character or sun; place it as a reaction label near the character's head with a small tail or alignment cue
Rethink the orange rim-glow on the character — it reads as a selection outline artifact rather than motivated light from the sun; match glow direction/color to the sun's actual position (upper-left)
Remove the faint horizontal banding lines across the mid-sky and dunes — they read as compression artifacts, not stylistic waves
Anchor the title card lower into the composition or add a subtle drop shadow to detach the dark pill from the darkening top-right gradient
Give the character a stronger ground contact shadow / slight scale-up — it floats slightly against the foreground dune and competes with the sun for focal attention
The character's raised arm overlaps the horizon line awkwardly — offset character or horizon so the pointing gesture has clean negative space
Large dead zone in the lower third (empty sand); either raise character slightly or add subtle dune texture/shadow detail to anchor the bottom
Sun/cloud cluster crowds the top-right edge and the cloud is clipped by frame — recompose so the glow reads fully at 9:16 crop
Tidy the scattered starburst lines around the scattering point — they read as random debris rather than a deliberate radial effect; reduce count and vary length intentionally
The exiting ray clips through the panel's right border with an abrupt color/opacity mismatch where it crosses the dark card — add a subtle refraction offset or exit glow to sell the transition

Bottom-left character and lower third of the frame sit in a dead zone relative to the diagram — either lift the character slightly toward the panel's gesture line or add a faint connecting accent to unify the composition
Clarify the diagram: the overlapping translucent circles read as mush at a glance—add a distinct outline or label dot to give the cluster a single legible focal point
Boost or remove the faint red diagonal line inside the panel; at phone size it is barely visible and reads as a rendering artifact
Rebalance composition: the bottom-right quadrant is a dead zone while the character huddles bottom-left—shift the figure toward center-left or enlarge the diagram panel to fill the frame
Lamp grid reads as scattered noise: 12 near-identical tiles with no clear focal lamp — enlarge the single orange lamp or spotlight it to create a guided eye path from title to grid to character
Blue-on-blue tiles (light blue squares over mid-blue bg with low-opacity cone glows) risk mushing together on a daylight phone — darken bg or add stronger rim/shadow separation on tiles

The bottom character and grid compete for attention with a dead-ish middle band of cone glows — tighten vertical rhythm so the grid clusters higher and the character breathes with clearer ground shadow contrast
Fill the bottom-left dead zone or reframe composition — lower third left of the character is empty sky, wasting ~30% of frame
Fix 'TOWARD SUN' contrast: light blue monospace on pale card will wash out on a 6-inch phone in daylight — darken text or darken card
Give the character a pointing target — arm gestures up-left into empty blue; aim it at the 'DEEP' card or the sun to complete the eye path
Reposition the NOT A MIRROR chip so it doesn't collide with the character's arm — the dark plate is cut by the elbow, weakening both elements
Fill the mid-left dead zone with a subtle secondary element (distant cloud or second small UFO) to balance the composition's left/right weight
Tighten the red underline swash to the chip's baseline width — it floats below the plate and reads as an unanchored artifact
Fill the large dead zone inside the dark screen panel — the red/blue dots are tiny and float in ~70% empty space; scale the gameplay elements to occupy the frame
Clarify the focal point: the beam and sun pull the eye to the top-left while the character and text sit at the bottom — reduce beam prominence or angle it toward the character
Add a subtle drop shadow or outline behind the cream caption text so it separates cleanly from the dark pill at small sizes

Fill the large dead zone in the mid-left band (between headline and ground) with a secondary background layer — drifting clouds, light shafts, or motion streaks — so the eye path from headline to character isn't a flat blue void
Drop the soft white halo/glow behind the headline — the mushy bloom reduces edge crispness and looks like a preset; flat text on that saturated blue would be cleaner and just as legible

Give the character a stronger anchor to the composition — it sits right-of-center with empty weight left; nudge it toward the rule-of-thirds intersection or add a foreground element (water splash, dock edge) to justify placement
